note: `FUN_1000_29c4` of `orig/g.exe` -- the `h` (drink one half-litre) and `mh` (drink until full or dry) routine -- the half-open image range `1000:29c4`..`1000:2c5e`, all 666 bytes and all 298 instructions, mapped by Task 41 from an aligned decode and never from a screen. Prose twin: `docs/re/beer.md`; classification twin: `data/beer_uncited.json`; re-derived from `orig/g.exe` by `tools/test_beer_arms.py`. `data/gym_arms.json` is the shape this follows. IT DECLARES NO `handlers` KEY ON PURPOSE: `tools/test_arms_artifacts.py`'s `test_the_corpus_is_every_arms_artifact_declaring_handlers` is a set equality over `data/*_arms.json` that declare `handlers`, and this artifact does not fit that file's schema -- it maps a CALLED ROUTINE bounded by its own function extent, not a verb-compare-bounded slice of `entry`, so `test_each_range_is_anchored_to_the_verb_compares_not_to_itself` has nothing to anchor. `data/den_arms.json` and `data/shop_arms.json` sit outside that corpus for the same kind of reason and keep their own suites; this one keeps `tools/test_beer_arms.py`. COVERAGE BOUNDARY: this artifact covers exactly that range. It says nothing about the four routines it CALLS (`0f78:02cd` the stack check, `0f78:0bd8` the Borland shortstring compare, `0eed:0000` Write and `0eed:01c2` WriteLn), whose bodies were not decoded here; `docs/re/character-sheet.md` and `docs/re/rtl.md` are the authorities for those four.
address_forms: `1000:xxxx` is a Ghidra label (Form A of `docs/re/METHODOLOGY.md`) and, because the game's code segment is the load base, its OFF is also the image offset. `20ae:xxxx` is DGROUP. `0eed:` and `0f78:` are Form B runtime segments. `cs_offset` is the image offset of a Pascal shortstring's LENGTH byte -- the exact immediate of the `mov di,imm16` that pushes it -- and `file_offset` is that plus the 0x18d0-byte MZ header, which is what `data/strings.json` keys on. ONE of the two call sites encodes a `rel16` that WRAPS: `1000:e966` (`0xe969 + 0x405b == 0x129c4`) reaches `1000:29c4` only modulo 64 KiB, which is the mistake `tools/re_derive.py`'s `near_calls_to` exists to avoid. `1000:4b00` calls BACKWARD (`0x4b03 - 0x213f == 0x29c4`) and needs no wrap. An earlier draft of this artifact said both wrapped; `tools/test_beer_arms.py` caught it.

range.note: Half-open, and it is the function extent `data/branches.json` records (`entry` 1000:29c4, `size` 666). `1000:2c5b ret 0x4` is the last instruction; `1000:2c5e` is the first byte of the 4275-byte literal run `docs/re/branches.md`'s undefined-run table lists at file 17710. The plan's brief writes the end as `1000:2c61`; the decode puts it at `1000:2c5e`, and 0x2c5e - 0x29c4 is exactly the 666 the same brief quotes.

census.method: tools/re_derive.py `near_calls_to` / `far_calls_to` over the whole image; the near scan compares the 16-bit-WRAPPED target.

sites.note: The shared street tail: `docs/re/gym.md` records that a `trn` miss and the gym's own `w` exit both land at 1000:e961, so this call is on every street line's path, not only the gym's. Its `rel16` is 0x405b and `0xe969 + 0x405b == 0x129c4`, so only the 16-bit wrap lands on the entry.
Combat's own input buffer, which is why beer works inside a fight. Its `rel16` is 0xdec1 = -0x213f and `0x4b03 - 0x213f == 0x29c4`: this one calls BACKWARD and does NOT wrap.

call_sites.difference_the_port_must_model: NONE. Both sites push `ds` and a DGROUP offset -- the same far-pointer shape -- and the routine's first act is to COPY the shortstring into its own frame (1000:29de `lds si,[bp+0x4]`), so the only thing that differs is which buffer the text came from. The routine reads no other caller state and writes only 20ae:38ac and 20ae:38c3, which are global. The port's two `self.beer(..)` call sites -- `grep -rn 'self\.beer(' src/` -- match that: one in `Game::run_command`, one in `Game::run_combat`, both passing only the `Beer` discriminant.

argument.what: one Pascal shortstring, by FAR pointer at [bp+0x4]; `1000:2c5b ret 0x4` pops it.
argument.frame: `sub sp,0x102` at 1000:29cf -- 256 bytes of buffer at [bp-0x100] plus one word at [bp-0x102].

es_is_ss.why: so the `stosb` / `rep movsb` destination is the STACK, not DGROUP -- which is what keeps them out of the store scan below.

stack_slot_bp_minus_0x102.what: hp (20ae:38ac) as it stood on entry, before a drop of beer is drunk.
stack_slot_bp_minus_0x102.written_once: An aligned decode of all 298 instructions finds exactly ONE instruction whose destination is this slot: 1000:2a14. So every read below sees the entry value.
stack_slot_bp_minus_0x102.stored_before_the_jaw_test: 1000:2a14 precedes 1000:2a18, so the snapshot exists even on the path that refuses to serve -- which is why the broken-jaw arm can fall into the tail at 1000:2baa and have the three compares mean `nothing was drunk`.

the_three_compares.decides: hp == hp0 -> skip the aggregate CS 0x2938 line
hp == hp0 -> skip CS 0x29b3 `ran out of beer`

stack_slot_bp_minus_0x102.three_way_versus_the_ports_two_way: The original re-READS 20ae:38ac at 1000:2bbf, 1000:2c06 and 1000:2c2f and re-compares it three times; `Game::beer` binds `healed` once and writes `if healed != 0 { .. } else if beer_dl == 0 { .. }`. The hoist is sound because nothing between the three reads writes 20ae:38ac: the store scan below finds the routine's only two writes to it at 1000:2a97 and 1000:2ae7, both inside the loop, and the only calls between the reads are `0eed:01c2`. The three-way is therefore three tests of TWO independent predicates -- (hp != hp0) and (beer <= 0) -- and the port's nesting reproduces all four of their combinations: healed -> summary; healed and dry -> `ran out`; not healed and dry -> `no beer`; not healed and beer left -> silence.

literal_pool.note: The 253 bytes immediately before the function entry are the routine's own literal pool, and they TILE: walking `p += 1 + img[p]` from 0x28c7 lands exactly on 0x29c4 with nothing left over. That is what makes `strings[]` a census rather than a list -- there is no room for a tenth literal. It is also the run `docs/re/branches.md`'s undefined-run table records at file 16791, length 253, `records 9`, `residual 0`.
literal_pool.strings_json_gap: `data/strings.json` is MISSING the two verb tokens (file 0x04197 `h` and 0x04199 `mh`, 5 bytes together). That is exactly the `1000:28c7 | 0x4197 | 5` row of `docs/re/branches.md`'s unaccounted-bytes table -- so the two artifacts corroborate each other, and the doc comment this task audits was right to cite the file offsets rather than `strings.json`.

the `mh` verb; compared at 1000:2a02 and again at 1000:2bb0

`no beer` -- pushed TWICE, by the in-loop arm (1000:2b4c, `h` only) and by the `mh` tail (1000:2c3f, nothing drunk AND beer exhausted)

gates.note: Every CONDITIONAL branch in the range, by aligned decode. `tools/test_beer_arms.py` requires this list to EQUAL the `class == "game"` branch set `data/branches.json` records for `func_entry == "1000:29c4"`, and `data/beer_uncited.json` to cover the same set -- no count is written by hand.

effects.note: The COMPLETE set of instructions in the range whose destination is an absolute DGROUP address. The routine writes hp and beer and nothing else -- not hpmax, not the jaw byte, not money. The two string-move instructions (1000:29e2 `stosb`, 1000:29e6 `rep movsb`) write ES:DI and ES is SS (see `argument.es_is_ss`), so they land on the frame; 1000:2a14 writes [bp-0x102], also the frame. Nothing else in the 298 instructions has a memory destination at all.

globals.identity: `python3 tools/re_query.py xrefs-to 20ae:38ac` accepts 74 references, 33 of them writes. The level-up `FUN_1000_2526` raises it and 20ae:38ae together (1000:2695/1000:2699 `inc` both, 1000:27c3/1000:27c8 `add 5` to both) while combat's damage line `1000:4783 sub [0x38ac],ax` moves only this one -- so this is the CURRENT value and 20ae:38ae the ceiling. `docs/re/save-format.md` and `src/persist.rs` agree.

`xrefs-to` accepts 59 references, 15 of them writes, and NONE of the 15 is in this range -- the beer routine only ever reads it, which is the ceiling behaviour. The `dec` at 1000:49ca and `sub 5` at 1000:4a30 in combat are the only writers that LOWER it.

`xrefs-to` accepts 17 references and exactly 5 writes, all immediate stores of 0 or 1: `mov byte [0x38b0],0x1` at 1000:47ee and 1000:4820 (combat) and `,0x0` at 1000:5031, 1000:b2ae and 1000:d558. `tools/test_gym_arms.py`'s `test_the_broken_jaw_byte_only_ever_holds_0_or_1` already defends that writer set; the beer routine's `cmp byte [0x38b0],0x1` at 1000:2a18 reads it the same way `Game::smoke`'s gate does.

`xrefs-to` accepts 19 references and 4 writes: this routine's `dec [0x38c3]` at 1000:2a51, the loot credit `add [0x38c3],ax` at 1000:5241, the shop purchase `inc [0x38c3]` at 1000:beb4 and `dec [0x38c3]` at 1000:db3a. Half-litres, not litres: the sheet prints `[0x38c3] div 2` with a `.5` for the odd half (`data/save_layout.json`, `docs/re/character-sheet.md`), and this routine spends exactly ONE unit per iteration for 5 hp.

tenths.shape: `idiv 2` / `xchg ax,dx` for the remainder, then `mov si,ax` / `shl ax,1` / `shl ax,1` / `add ax,si` for the *5, then `idiv 10` / `xchg ax,dx`.

litres_and_tenths.note: The `mod 10` is real and is at 1000:2ad5..1000:2adb, 1000:2b2b..1000:2b31 and 1000:2bf9..1000:2bff -- three copies. `Game::beer_numbers` writes `(beer_dl % 2) * 5` WITHOUT it, which is not a divergence for any value a `u16` can hold (the product is 0 or 5, and `x mod 10 == x` there) but is inconsistent with `src/character_sheet.rs`, which does spell the `% 10`. Recorded as an observation, not a defect: `grep -n '% 2) \* 5' src/game.rs src/character_sheet.rs`.

arithmetic.no_other_arithmetic: No `mul`, no `imul`, no `div`, no shift other than the two `shl ax,1` of the *5 idiom, and no `Random`. The drink is a flat 5 hp or a top-up to hpmax; nothing is scaled and nothing is rolled.

draws.method: Two independent sweeps, both required: (1) the aligned decode of all 298 instructions holds exactly four distinct CALL targets -- `0f78:02cd`, `0f78:0bd8`, `0eed:0000`, `0eed:01c2` -- and `0f78:114b` is not among them; (2) a byte scan for the five-byte `Random` far call `9a 4b 11 78 0f` over [0x29c4, 0x2c62) returns zero hits. The byte scan alone would be a check that cannot fail, so the same scan over the whole image is required to return the 86 sites `docs/re/METHODOLOGY.md` names -- that is the negative control.
draws.consequence: `tests/combat_sequence.rs` and `tests/wander_sequence.rs` must stay green draw-for-draw across any change to `Game::beer`; movement in either is a bug, never a rebaseline.

spans.name: prologue
spans.note: `push bp` / `mov bp,sp`, the `0f78:02cd` stack check for a 0x102-byte frame, `sub sp,0x102`, then ES:=SS and a `lodsb`/`stosb`/`rep movsb` copy of the caller's shortstring (far pointer at [bp+0x4]) into the local buffer at [bp-0x100].

spans.name: the two token compares
spans.note: `"h"` at 1000:29f0 then `"mh"` at 1000:2a02, both through `0f78:0bd8` on the local copy. 1000:2a0e `jmp 0x2c58` is the neither-token return: no store, no output.

spans.name: hp snapshot and the jaw gate
spans.note: 1000:2a11/1000:2a14 copy 20ae:38ac into [bp-0x102] -- the value the whole `mh` tail compares against -- and 1000:2a18 tests the broken-jaw byte.

spans.name: the broken-jaw refusal
spans.note: CS 0x28cc through `0eed:01c2` with five zeroed format words, then 1000:2a38 `jmp 0x2baa` -- into the TAIL, not to the return.

spans.name: loop top: the two continue gates
spans.note: hp < hpmax (1000:2a3e/1000:2a42, SIGNED) else `jmp 0x2b67`; beer > 0 (1000:2a47/1000:2a4c, SIGNED) else `jmp 0x2b3a`.

spans.name: spend one half-litre, then size the drink
spans.note: `dec [0x38c3]`, then shortfall := hpmax - hp and `cmp ax,5` at 1000:2a5c.

spans.name: the partial arm -- shortfall < 5
spans.note: `h` writes CS 0x28fd through `0eed:0000` (no newline) with the shortfall; hp := hpmax (1000:2a94/1000:2a97); `h` writes CS 0x2914 with hp, hpmax, beer div 2 and ((beer mod 2) * 5) mod 10.

spans.name: the flat arm -- shortfall >= 5
spans.note: `add word [0x38ac],0x5`, then `h` writes the combined CS 0x2938 with the literal 5 and the same four trailing fields.

spans.name: the no-beer arm
spans.note: reached only from 1000:2a4e. `h` writes CS 0x2970; `mh` writes nothing here and lets the loop-continue test end the loop.

spans.name: the already-healthy arm
spans.note: reached only from 1000:2a44. CS 0x297c UNCONDITIONALLY -- no `h`/`mh` gate -- then 1000:2b80 `jmp 0x2c58` returns, so this arm never reaches the tail.

spans.name: the loop-continue test
spans.note: `h` leaves after one unit (1000:2b93 / 1000:2b95); `mh` loops back through 1000:2ba7 `jmp 0x2a3b` while hp < hpmax AND beer > 0.

spans.name: the tail's `mh` gate
spans.note: 1000:2bb0 compares the buffer against `"mh"`; 1000:2bbc `jmp 0x2c58` is `h`'s exit, so everything below is `mh`-only.

spans.name: tail 1 of 3 -- the aggregate line
spans.note: hp != [bp-0x102] -> CS 0x2938 with hp - hp0 in the first field.

spans.name: epilogue
spans.note: `mov sp,bp` / `pop bp` / `ret 0x4` -- the 4 bytes are the caller's far pointer.

sweeps.note: Every one of these is the aligned decode's own count, asserted by `tools/test_beer_arms.py` against a fresh walk of `orig/g.exe`.

globals_are_a_measurement: `globals[]` is every DGROUP address the range touches, not a list of the four someone noticed. `tools/test_beer_arms.py`'s `test_the_recorded_globals_are_every_dgroup_address_the_range_touches` sweeps every absolute-memory operand in the aligned decode and asserts SET EQUALITY against the `ds` keys below, so a fifth global -- including one that is only READ, which the effects sweep cannot see because it only buckets writes -- reds the test. The same sweep also requires every instruction carrying an absolute-memory operand to fall in the READ or the WRITE bucket, so an unrecognised shape fails loudly instead of being counted as neither. This artifact is outside `tools/test_arms_artifacts.py`'s corpus, which is where `test_the_dgroup_addresses_touched_are_the_recorded_globals` lives for the three handler maps; that exclusion is why the sweep had to be written here rather than inherited.
